attribution_limitations: Month counts of conventional treatment do not map consistently to the printed calendar dates (e.g., 12th month = April 2023 in the Fig. 1 caption, 24th month = September 2024 in Table 1/Fig. 1B, initial assessment September 2022, and 36th month = 6th month of memantine = April 2025 in Table 2).
Dates of the CSF analysis, diagnosis confirmation and start of immunotherapy are not stated; April 2023 is attached only to the repeat MRI.
Fig. 1B caption says decreased hippocampal intensity is correlating with clinical impairment, whereas the text reports psychiatric improvement but persistent cognitive deficits.

The statement of improvements exceeding 50% in some BRIEF-P subscales does not state its baseline; Table 1 values between the 24th month and the 6th month after memantine onset do not obviously exceed 50% for all named subscales.

Causality of memantine for the improvements is explicitly not established; conventional immunotherapy and psychotropics continued, spontaneous resolution and psychosocial support changes are acknowledged covariates.
Nausea and hyperactivity are called mild side effects without naming the causative drug; memantine is implied by context only. The within-a-week resolution is stated in the Discussion.
It is not stated whether the three additional immunotherapy cycles repeated IVMP, IVIG or both, or their order relative to rituximab.
The Abstract states psychiatric improvement in 6 months while the Case section states substantial improvement by the 18th month; the anchor of the 6 months is not given.
The parenthetical (in February 2022) follows lip herpes; whether it also dates the recent viral respiratory infection is not explicit. Both are caregiver-reported.

Discussion sentences describing other published cases (Liu et al. eight patients, Finke et al. nine patients, Hinkle et al. three adolescent girls, Mohammad et al., Bradley) and generic memantine dosing are literature and not facts about the index patient.

The authors evaluate WISC-R subtests related to verbal IQ (specifically memory) as indicators of improvement, but Table 2 shows digit span unchanged (5 to 5) and arithmetic and comprehension/judgement slightly lower (8 to 7; 10 to 9).
